change: Dotted updates for dynamic/fixed array slices, stepped ranges, stored ranges, masks and index lists. Capture receiver indices, source values and selectors before the RHS; freeze open bounds; reacquire writeback storage. Scope the source snapshot to selection, avoiding an unnecessary full-array COW detach.
validation: Independent C bootstrap: 876 numeric, compound assignment, slice/index and formatter checks passed in 22.68s. The same broad checks passed before the lifetime change; 190 focused checks then covered that change. Ruff and git diff --check passed.
coverage: saved value copies, managed strings and allocation cleanup
each parent index, range endpoint and selector evaluated once in order
RHS resizes the parent array, replaces the source or mutates the selector
empty ranges, index lists and masks; duplicate indices use old values and last write wins
constant targets rejected; invalid bounds, shape, mask length, zero step and short resized destination fail

lifetime_probe.limits: An implementation-development comparison for the new feature, not a speedup over the previous committed language (which rejected dotted selection updates). 1024 updates of two elements in a 65536-element array, allocation included; asserts unchanged neighboring elements and final results.

limits: Matrix slices and dotted prefix operators remain unsupported.
Selected values and output are materialized; no claim of allocation-free updates.
